proseChanges.summary: **Inbound mail contact lookups at scale:** an inbound mail's contact lookups by address (the blocked-sender check, the sender's and each Cc's contact, the new-contact guard, and a reply's sender through a reply address or from a preferred notification address) search an index of the address instead of walking every contact of a large imported workspace, and a member reply's send issues each recipient's reply address by reading the conversation's own contact and participants by key. An ordinary inbound mail on a workspace of about 160,000 contacts reads about 1,400 rows instead of about 490,000, and the send of a reply about 180 instead of about 320,000. Every lookup matches exactly the contacts it matched before. Apply `322_contact_address_lookup.sql` after 321. **Fixes — conversations whose text repeats help-site passages no longer overload D1:** in a large imported workspace whose crawled help site shares boilerplate across hundreds of pages, a conversation open, thread read, inbox list or search, inbound mail or member reply whose text repeats such passages evaluated the knowledge reference policy once per (passage, reader, page) occurrence, and looked up each page's current version by walking the whole published version: over a million D1 rows per evaluation, several evaluations per open, and `503` once opens came in a row. The policy now decides each passage for each reader with one search that stops at the first page that decides it, and a page of the published version is its own current page, so a 16-passage open reads over a hundred times fewer rows. What each reader is shown, and what admission and outbound mail allow, is unchanged. One limit remains: on a very large imported desk whose older crawl version's documents no longer have their URLs, one evaluation can still read many rows until the planned index for older crawl versions exists, and this release does not remove that. Our recommendation to operators: keep mail off on a host with imported help documents until further notice. **Fixes — the help-article `500` reached back to v0.4.15:** the knowledge reference policy code that real D1 refuses was byte-identical in v0.4.15, v0.4.16 and v0.4.17 and unchanged in v0.4.18, so an installation of any of them with published help articles answered `500` when a member opened, or searched the inbox for, a conversation whose text overlaps an article, and on inbound mail that quotes one. v0.4.19 fixed it and this release keeps that fix; the v0.4.19 notes named only v0.4.17 and v0.4.18. **Erasing a teammate retires them from the Business roster:** erasing a teammate account now also removes them from the roster their Business signed: their team row and their entry in the stored Business settings document are removed in the same transaction as the erasure, their policy references in local agent policy are retired the same way, and only a value-free tombstone (digests of the roster address and Business member id with the invite number they had) is kept. The Business's next signed revision that still lists an erased teammate applies as retired: every other value and teammate applies, and the erased person gets no account, no invitation and no row until the Business sends a larger invite number. Before, a signed revision listing an erased teammate was refused with `member_erased` and the person's hash-named roster row and renamed document entry stayed. A teammate erased by an earlier release leaves the roster at the Business's next revision, listed or not. Adopts rer 0.2.107 and its Base copy. One corner remains, in Base's `retireGone` handling: a teammate erased by v0.4.19 or an earlier release and left unlisted by the Business, then listed by a later revision at the same invite number with their real address and no member id, can get a fresh account and an invitation where the earlier release refused with `member_erased`; a Business that sends member ids is fully fenced, and Base tracks this as a follow-up. **Fixes — `rer deploy` names the mail secrets:** the deployment declaration now lists the seven outbound-mail secret names (`EMAIL_PROVIDER`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `EMAIL_API_KEY_NAME`, `MAILGUN_DOMAIN`, `MAILGUN_REGION`, `MAILGUN_SENDING_KEY`, `MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY`), so `rer deploy` prints one line naming the mail secrets bound on the Worker instead of the false "Outbound email is off"; an offline `rer deploy --dry-run` lists the seven names and says the bound secrets were not read. No behaviour change for mail itself. **Migrations:** `322_contact_address_lookup.sql`, `323_business_retired.sql`. Apply once, in this order, after `321_legacy_import_files.sql` and BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic. `322_contact_address_lookup.sql` is additive and creates two indexes on contacts. `323_business_retired.sql` is additive and creates one empty table, `bs_retired`; without it, erasing a teammate refuses with `business_roster_missing_table:bs_retired`.

proseChanges.now: v0.4.20 adds migrations 322_contact_address_lookup.sql and 323_business_retired.sql, adopts rer 0.2.107, and carries the inbound mail lookup index and the cheaper knowledge reference search. Published upgrade baselines are v0.4.19 and v0.4.18.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Update from v0.4.19 without resetting. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.107. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. Apply the missing migrations once, in filename order, BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic: 322_contact_address_lookup.sql, then 323_business_retired.sql (a v0.4.19 or v0.4.18 installation applies exactly those two; v0.4.18 has migrations through 321). Earlier installations apply every missing published migration in filename order first (v0.4.17 needs 321_legacy_import_files.sql, then `node scripts/legacy-import/upgrade.mjs --project <legacy project id>` once per workspace imported from legacy, as the v0.4.18 notes describe; v0.4.16 also needs 320_legacy_import_work_repair.sql); retain each migration's buyer steps. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. No reset, cutover or production deployment is part of this release. Live-provider qualification and owner cutover remain separate.

migrations.buyerSteps: Back up D1 first; apply once after 321_legacy_import_files.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: creates two indexes on contacts (contacts_address_lookup on (project_id, lower(email)) and contacts_preferred_address_lookup on (project_id, lower(json_extract(metadata_json,'$.provided_email')))), so an inbound mail's contact lookups by address search an index instead of walking every contact of the workspace; no row changes and nothing is read, sent or queued. On a workspace of about 160,000 contacts it applies in under a second.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 322_contact_address_lookup.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: creates the empty bs_retired table (value-free tombstones of team members erased from the installation: domain-separated SHA-256 digests of the roster address and the Business member id, with the invite number each had; never a name or address); no existing row changes and nothing is read, sent or queued. Without it, erasing a team member refuses with business_roster_missing_table:bs_retired. Nothing else to do: a team member erased by an earlier release leaves the Business roster at the Business's next signed revision.

pendingMigrations.buyerSteps: Back up D1 first; apply once after 323_business_retired.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: creates one index on knowledge_documents (knowledge_documents_version_url on (version_id, url)), so the knowledge reference policy's check that an older crawl version's page still has a current twin at the same URL searches an index instead of walking every page of the published version; no row changes and nothing is read, sent or queued. On a crawled site of a few thousand pages it applies in under a second.
